_purpose: UC3 Excalibur Job 3 -- batch load + reconciliation + heal/append into bronze. Section 6 of the build prompt, governed by docs/UC3/BUILD_CONTRACT.md. PURE CONFIGURATION: no hand-written comparison, MERGE or hash exists anywhere in this build. The three ingestion_flows land the dated batch CSVs into flowx.staging.<table>_batch; the three reconciliation_flows compare each batch table against the Job 2 bronze target on the composite PK and heal the difference back into bronze through the framework's own append lane.

_provenance.governance_source: docs/UC3/{PHYSICAL_DEVICE,CUSTOMER,SUBSCRIBER}_DDL.csv -- every PK, Drop(DF)/Null(DF) flag, type and tag value below was read from these sheets, never hand-typed. Header quirks handled: 'Sesnitive Columns' is misspelled in the source and PHYSICAL_DEVICE spells the tier flag 'csql.securedro' (no underscore); both are read verbatim and emitted as csql_secured_ro.
_provenance.column_metadata_reuse: Column-level governance is NOT duplicated from Job 2. The bronze tables flowx.bronze.* are owned and tagged by dfg_uc3_excalibur_streaming_cdc (onboarding/uc3/uc3_excalibur_streaming_cdc.json). This spec tags only the staging tables it actually creates, and applies the identical Null(DF)=Y forced-NULL rules from BUILD_CONTRACT.md section 4 so a batch row can never re-introduce a value that streaming nulled out.
_provenance.sibling_spec: onboarding/uc3/uc3_excalibur_streaming_cdc.json (dfg_uc3_excalibur_streaming_cdc) -- read for consistency, never edited by this spec's author.

_hash_specification.algorithm: SHA-256, hex (framework canonical; NOT base64 - see capability map 2.1)
_hash_specification.ordering: alphabetical, resolved by cdc/comparison_columns.py at runtime
_hash_specification._note: Declared here for audit only. Nothing in this spec implements it: cdc/hashing.py is the single canonical implementation and is never rebuilt locally. The batch staging tables are APPEND, so they do NOT carry __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value -- which is exactly why every reconciliation_flows[].source_config below sets hash_precomputed:false and each target sets it true (the bronze side already carries them from Job 2's CDC dispatch).

subscriber.reason: Drop(Specific to Data Fabric)=Y in SUBSCRIBER_DDL.csv. Both columns also carry Null(DF)=Y, and Drop wins (BUILD_CONTRACT.md section 4): a dropped column cannot also be a nulled column because it does not exist in the target. They therefore appear in NO data_standardization_sql anywhere in this spec.

hash_value.reason: Target-only column in all three sheets; supplied by the framework as __framework_hash_value when generate_hash_columns is true. No hash_value column is ever created.

_batch_date_grain_finding: Section 6.1 asks for the four counts per batch_date. This is NOT expressible in one reconciliation flow: reconciliation/graph_registration.py::_counts_query is a hard-coded ungrouped .agg() producing exactly ONE row per (flow, target, run), and ALLOWED_RECONCILIATION_FLOW_KEYS admits no group-by/grain key. transform_sql does not help -- it reshapes the miss set before append (appender.py::apply_transform_sql), never the metrics. The only config-expressible per-date grain is source_config.filter_condition, i.e. one flow per (table, batch_date) = 12 flows with dates hard-coded into the spec. That is rejected here as spec-time date pinning. This spec therefore reconciles the WHOLE batch table per table (3 flows), and the per-batch_date breakdown is reported as a capability gap rather than hand-rolled.

ingestion_flows._table: physical_device -- 31 business columns; PK is 4 columns wide (BUILD_CONTRACT.md section 3).
ingestion_flows.source_description: Dated Excalibur PHYSICAL_DEVICE batch extracts, one batch_date=YYYY-MM-DD partition folder per set (2026-08-01..04).
ingestion_flows._why_append: Staging keeps all four dated sets side by side (BUILD_CONTRACT.md section 10), so this is a pure APPEND landing table -- NOT a CDC target. cdc_operation_column/columns_to_exclude/generate_hash_columns are deliberately absent: the validator scopes them to SCD strategies, and the batch side's hashes are computed by the reconciliation engine itself (hash_precomputed:false below).

ingestion_flows._table: customer -- 90 business columns; single-column PK, SCD2 in bronze.
ingestion_flows.source_description: Dated Excalibur CUSTOMER batch extracts, one batch_date=YYYY-MM-DD partition folder per set (2026-08-01..04).

ingestion_flows._table: subscriber -- 133 business columns; ctn_password/sub_password are DROPPED (Drop wins over Null), so they appear in no data_standardization_sql and carry no column_tags here.
ingestion_flows.source_description: Dated Excalibur SUBSCRIBER batch extracts, one batch_date=YYYY-MM-DD partition folder per set (2026-08-01..04).

reconciliation_flows._intent: Compare the whole physical_device batch staging table against the Job 2 bronze target on the composite PK, publish the four counts, and heal missing/drifted rows back into bronze through the framework's own append lane. No comparison, MERGE or hash is written by hand anywhere.

customer is SCD2 in bronze. Batch rows older than what bronze already holds must NOT regress history -- that is the framework SCD engine's job via sequence_by_column: sys_update_date on the Job 2 flow, and is deliberately NOT special-cased here.

subscriber -- 2-column composite PK in declared order (subscriber_no, customer_id), matching BUILD_CONTRACT.md section 3 exactly. Order is load-bearing: it is the basis of __framework_hash_key on the bronze side.

_iceberg_deferral: REMOVED 2026-09-05 (Phase C): table_properties.enable_iceberg_read_uniformity. Databricks does not support Iceberg reads on STREAMING TABLES or MATERIALIZED VIEWS via IcebergCompatV2 -- see docs 'Read Delta Lake tables with Iceberg clients': "Iceberg reads can't be enabled on materialized views or streaming tables using IcebergCompatV2". Three genuine framework defects were found and FIXED en route (delta.enableIcebergCompatV2, delta.columnMapping.mode=name, and the deletion-vector prerequisite), and those fixes remain correct for batch_table targets. The supported path for pipeline-managed streaming tables is IcebergCompatV3, which additionally requires DBR 17.3+, pipeline setting pipelines.externalMetadata.enabled=true, and delta.enableChangeDataFeed=false -- the last conflicting directly with FlowX setting CDF=true for every CDC-dispatched strategy. Deferred by explicit user decision; tracked as a known gap.
_compare_columns_rationale: compare_columns MUST be declared explicitly. reconciliation/matcher.py: 'None/empty means key-presence-only matching ... every co-present key counts as matched regardless of its other column values' -- which made value_drift_count structurally 0 on the first Job 3 run, even though 40 of the 72 overlapping rows per table genuinely differ. The set mirrors the 5.1 hash spec: every non-dropped business column EXCEPT the primary keys and the two timestamps (sys_creation_date, sys_update_date), plus src_deleted_flg excluded as the CDC control column. Derived from the DDL sheets, never hand-typed.
_hash_precomputed_rationale: target hash_precomputed MUST be false here. It was true, which told reconciliation to trust the bronze table's stored __framework_hash_value verbatim. That hash was computed by the CDC engine over ITS resolved comparison set (every non-PK column, including sys_creation_date/sys_update_date and src_deleted_flg), whereas reconciliation hashes the source over this flow's compare_columns (87 cols, timestamps and the CDC control column excluded). matcher.py states the precondition plainly: 'the upstream flow's primary_keys must be this flow's match_keys, and its resolved comparison columns this flow's compare_columns ... when they disagree nothing errors -- the hashes simply never match and every row reports as drifted.' That is exactly what happened: matched_count collapsed to 0 and value_drift_count absorbed all 72 overlapping keys. With hash_precomputed=false both sides are hashed inline from the SAME compare_columns, so matched vs drifted is computed on like-for-like input.
